elements.element: Renewal occurs automatically for 12-month periods (preferred alternative to mutual-written-agreement-only renewal)
elements.evidence: "The Agreement shall be renewed automatically for an additional period of 12 months at the end of the Initial Period"; "Such renewal shall recur automatically for further 12-month periods"

elements.element: Customer may opt out of renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "no renewal shall take effect if Licensee gives not less than 30 days' notice of non-renewal prior to the end of the then-current period"

elements.element: Vendor reminder of upcoming renewal at least 60 days before renewal
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall notify Licensee of the upcoming renewal not less than 60 days prior to the end of the then-current period"

elements.element: Renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: "fees for any renewal period shall not increase by more than the lesser of the increase in CPI and 3%"

elements.element: Automatic renewal with non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: "not less than 30 days' notice of non-renewal" — 30-day window is within the 60-day maximum
"shall not increase by more than the lesser of the increase in CPI and 3%" — 3% is below the 5% ceiling

reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred automatic-renewal branch are present in operative text: 12-month automatic renewal, Licensee 30-day opt-out, Licensor 60-day reminder, and an uplift cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
The fallback is also satisfied on its own terms (30-day window ≤ 60 days; 3% ≤ 5%), so the clause is compliant at the locked preferred level.

Minimal: one targeted sentence replacement removing the Licensor-option seven-year renewal (which was the offending term) plus one concise sub-clause carrying the three remaining mechanics; no unrelated sentence rewritten and no new exceptions or boilerplate added.

Unrelated commercial terms are untouched — the Licensor breach-termination right, retained payment rights, sub-clause II's 45-day mutual-written extension and sub-clause III's mutual-written further extensions all remain effective.

Note (rationale only, not a deviation): sub-clause II's mandatory mutual-written extension of the Initial Period sits awkwardly beside the new automatic renewal, but that tension pre-existed the redline (it equally conflicted with the Licensor's option renewal) and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced; a short conforming cross-reference ("subject to Article IV.I") could be added if the team wants full alignment.
